newsitem.title: UK: Quiet start to week on UK physical grain markets.
newsitem.headline: Quiet start to week on UK physical grain markets.

text.p: Business got off to a slow start on the UK physical grain markets on Monday with buyers showing little interest and sellers looking for an excuse to push the market higher.
"Buyers are well covered and as soon as sellers see sterling ease they want to add one stg to the price, so we have stalemate," said a trader.
Others said they expected more sellers to appear if prices went higher, but they were unlikely to find buyers.
"We get the feeling there is an awful of business waiting to be done, but buyers can afford to wait," said one trader.
Traders reported no business or even close markets on the fob market.
In the delivered sector most of the business was in feed wheat with only a few trades in feed barley and nothing reported in mill wheat.
In East Anglia feed wheat was trading between 95 and 96 stg for January depending on area while in the south west Feb was fatching 97 stg and Apr/Jun 100 stg a tonne.
Feed barley in east Anglia was trading at 100 stg for Apr/Jun.
